The position $y(t)$ of a particle oscillating with simple harmonic motion is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+36y=0,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. What is the period of the oscillation?

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Period of a Simple Harmonic Oscillation
examples.problem:
The position $y(t)$ of a particle oscillating with simple harmonic motion is governed by the equation

$$
y'' + 100y = 0,
$$

where $t > 0$ is the time, in seconds. What is the period of the oscillation?
examples.worked_solution:
The simple harmonic motion (SHM) equation is

$$
y'' + \omega^2 y = 0
$$

where the period $T$ is given by

$$
T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\omega^2 = 100\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \omega = 10,
$$

so the period (in seconds) is

$$
T = \dfrac{2\pi}{10} = \dfrac{\pi}{5}\,\textrm{s}.
$$

feedback.problem: The function $y(t)$ gives the position of a particle at time $t.$ Which of the following equations represents a situation in which the particle is undergoing simple harmonic motion?
feedback.worked_solution:
The simple harmonic motion (SHM) equation is

$$
{y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=0.
$$

We can see that the only equation that represents SHM is

$$
{y}^{″}+2y=0.
$$

In the above case:

$$
{\omega }^{2}=2\,⟹\,\omega =\sqrt{2}
$$
